poems: Elevenses is a real word. The English have been managing this hour for two hundred years and still call it a snack.
The bagel was breakfast. This is a second, unrelated bagel.
A folding table outside the fire station. Coleman cooler, hand-lettered sign, four kinds of soda.
11:03. Someone in the row behind you unwraps something that takes eight seconds to unwrap.
Deposit slip, ballpoint on a chain, no hurry.
Thaw the chicken now, or admit at six that it is a pasta night.

What was going to be a productive morning
is now going to be a productive afternoon.
The afternoon has not been consulted.
Somewhere a school is already at lunch.
Two ladders, one van, a radio playing the same eight songs since seven.
You are not hungry. You are bored in a specific location.
11:10 is when the pot of coffee turns to tar.
11:11. The wish is that lunch were sooner.

Errands, in order of dread:
pharmacy
DMV
return without a receipt
the post office at noon
In the infusion chair, the good blanket is the one from home.
A cake box on the break room counter, a name in marker, nobody has cut it.
11:15. The tradespeople are on their second break and their fifth hour.
Gulls in the strip mall parking lot, waiting.
Hunger, noun: the argument lost slowly between eleven and noon.
The plan made at nine is still technically alive.
11:19. A courthouse hallway. Everyone is early for something they did not choose.
Overheard: I can do Thursday, but not the Thursday after.
Wet concrete, a rake mark, one cat print.
Half the planet is asleep right now and you resent them slightly.

SUB TOTAL 4.25
TAX .34
CASH 5.00
CHANGE .41
THANK YOU COME AGAIN
11:24, and the dog has been let out twice already, for form's sake.

The email you have not answered
is being answered by somebody else
in a tone you would not have chosen.
This is fine.
A woman on a bench outside the library, eating almonds one at a time.
11:27 is not lunch. 11:27 is reconnaissance.
The retirees have finished at the bank and moved on to the hardware store, where they will be a while.
Somewhere a bell, somewhere a whistle, and a thousand kids stand up at once.
If it's Sunday, brunch is winding down. If it's Tuesday, nothing is winding down.
Onion rolls cooling on a rack behind glass.
Your stomach has opinions and no data.
A leaf blower. Then no leaf blower. Then a leaf blower.

11:34, and someone has said let's take this offline
about a thing that was never online.
Drink water. It will not fix the hunger, but it buys eleven minutes.
The night shift is four hours down and dreaming about the same hallway.

A traffic cone lies on its side.
No one has the authority.
The gym at this hour belongs to people with schedules nobody else can imagine.
11:39. Somebody microwaves fish. The floor will discuss this until three.

Three tomatoes on a windowsill,
one turning,
one turned,
one still lying about it.
The pharmacy says twenty minutes. It has said twenty minutes since ten.
A tarp, four bricks, a boat nobody sails.
You have opened the refrigerator. Nothing in it is new since eight.
Sign taped inside the glass: BACK AT 11:45. It is 11:44.
11:45 is the earliest defensible lunch, and defense will be required.
Church parking lot, empty, striped, one van with a wheelchair lift.
A new father, off shift, asleep through the exact middle of the morning.
The mail truck stops, does not stop, stops.
Everything scheduled for this morning has eleven minutes to become a lie.

Deli counter.
Your number, 74.
Their number, 61.
Thirteen sandwiches of patience.
Scaffolding, a radio, a man singing the wrong words with total confidence.
Eight minutes of dignity remain.
A crossing guard's stop sign leans in the school office, off duty until three.
The soup is either lunch or a decision to have a real lunch later.
11:55. Somebody says grab something, and three chairs move at once.
A housekeeping cart parked outside 1104, the door propped with a shoe.
Wash the pan while the water is still hot. That is the only advice.
Nothing important will be started in the next two minutes. This is understood.
11:59, and the break room microwave begins its long shift.
